projector-screen.definition: A flat surface designed to display an enlarged image from a projector.
projector-screen.exampleUsage: The presentation appeared on the projector screen.

laser-pointer.definition: A small device that produces a narrow laser beam for pointing; it must never be aimed at eyes, people, vehicles, or aircraft.
laser-pointer.exampleUsage: The meeting room follows strict safety rules for laser pointers.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.
microphone.exampleUsage: The microphone picked up the speaker’s voice during the meeting.

camera.definition: Equipment for taking photographs (usually consisting of a lightproof box with a lens at one end and light-sensitive film at the other).

flip-chart.definition: Used for presentations, a flip chart has large sheets attached along the top so a speaker can reveal information one page at a time.

marker.definition: A pen with a broad tip used for writing on paper or a board.

remote-clicker.definition: A handheld wireless control used to change presentation slides from a distance.
remote-clicker.exampleUsage: The presenter used a remote clicker to advance the slides.

name-plate.definition: A small sign displaying a person's name, role, or organization.
name-plate.exampleUsage: Each seat had a name plate.

agenda.definition: A list of matters to be taken up (as at a meeting).

staff-meeting.definition: A meeting where employees discuss work, plans, or shared concerns.

board-meeting.definition: A formal session in which an organization’s directors review its affairs, set long-term plans, and ensure that it is properly governed.

one-on-one.definition: Involving or intended for direct communication between two people and no one else.

brainstorm.definition: To generate and share ideas freely to solve a problem or plan work.

stand-up.definition: A short team meeting, often held standing, to share progress and obstacles.

town-hall.definition: A meeting where staff or community members hear updates and ask questions.

workshop.definition: A practical group session for learning, discussing, or developing ideas.

webinar.definition: A live seminar held online allows participants to learn and interact in real time.

kick-off.definition: A planned meeting or ceremony that officially marks the beginning of an event, project, process, or active period.

retrospective.definition: A meeting to review completed work and identify improvements for the future.

slide-deck.definition: A collection of digital slides prepared for a presentation.

handout.definition: A printed or digital document given to participants for reference.

report.definition: A document presenting information or findings about a subject.

chart.definition: A visual display of information, such as numbers, comparisons, or trends.

graph.definition: A diagram showing relationships between quantities or changes in values.

diagram.definition: A drawing intended to explain how something works.

flowchart.definition: A diagram of the sequence of operations in a computer program or an accounting system.

timeline.definition: A display or plan showing events or tasks in time order.

spreadsheet.definition: A file that organises information in rows and columns for calculations and records.

dashboard.definition: A display that brings together important information about work or performance.

present.definition: To explain information or ideas to an audience.

discuss.definition: To consider or examine in speech or writing.

vote.definition: To indicate a choice or preference in a decision-making process.

approve.definition: To officially accept or agree to a plan or request.

reject.definition: To not accept something given or offered.

table.definition: To postpone discussion of a proposal in American English, or formally submit it in British English.

follow-up.definition: To take further action after an earlier discussion or request.
follow-up.exampleUsage: The team scheduled a follow-up after the meeting.

assign.definition: To give a task or responsibility to a person or group.

minute.definition: To record the main points and decisions of a meeting.

adjourn.definition: To break from a meeting or gathering.

zoom.definition: A video meeting service used for remote calls.

teams.definition: A Microsoft service for online meetings and team messages.

screen-share.definition: To let other participants view the contents of a device’s screen.
screen-share.exampleUsage: The presenter used screen share to show the document.

mute.definition: To turn off or reduce sound from a microphone or instrument.

unmute.definition: To turn a microphone or device's sound back on.
unmute.exampleUsage: Please unmute your microphone before asking the question.

chat.definition: A space for exchanging written messages during an online meeting.

breakout-room.definition: A smaller physical or virtual meeting space used by a subset of participants for separate discussion.
breakout-room.exampleUsage: The workshop divided participants into a breakout room.

waiting-room.definition: A virtual or physical area where participants wait before being admitted to a meeting.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Online guests remained in the waiting room until admitted.

recording.definition: A stored copy of video or sound that can be played again later.

virtual-background.definition: A digital image or effect displayed behind a person during a video call instead of the real surroundings.
virtual-background.exampleUsage: She selected a plain virtual background for the meeting.

speaker.definition: A device that converts an electrical audio signal into sound.
